title: Personal scratch: key throttling breadcrumbs
content:
Context:
- Personal troubleshooting scratchpad while investigating sporadic 401s followed by lots of 429s for a single customer API key (prod).
- Customer first reported failures 2026-03-04 21:00 UTC; intermittent since then, bursty.
- Hypothesis: either key rotated unexpectedly, or a miscount in quota accounting causing premature throttling, or aggressive global token-level throttling incorrectly applied to org.

Symptoms observed (high-level):
- Initial wave: 401 Unauthorized for ~30s across multiple endpoints for same key.
- Follow-up wave: mostly 429 Too Many Requests; Retry-After header sometimes present, sometimes missing.
- In client metrics, spikes in latency and connection retries during timeframe.

Commands and requests I ran (local repro and probes):
1) Simple curl auth probe (valid key known):
   curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_customerABCxyz" 
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
     -d '{"input":"hello"}' 
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
   Observed (sample):
     * Connected to api.redwood.ai
     < HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
     < x-request-id: req_7f3a2b
     < content-type: application/json
     {"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found"}}

2) Re-run immediately (same key) repeatedly (5x) -> 2nd run 200 OK, 3rd run 429, 4th 429 (Retry-After: 10)
3) Probe without Authorization header -> 401 Unauthorized with error type missing_auth (expected)
4) Probe with a different valid key from same org (sk_live_customerDEF) -> 200 OK consistently
5) Curl to /v1/usage endpoint (admin test key):
   curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_admin_test" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/usage?key=sk_live_customerABCxyz
   Observed: returns usage numbers; however, daily_quota_consumed spikes suspiciously in the 401 window (see metrics excerpt below).

Observed response headers & bodies (samples aggregated):
- 401 responses: sometimes include x-request-id, sometimes not. Body: {"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found"}}
- 429 responses: headers sometimes include: Retry-After: 10, x-rate-limit-limit: 60000, x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
- Other 429s show no Retry-After and no rate-limit headers (this feels like a gateway-level 429 vs application-level).

Server-side breadcrumbs (pulled from logs around req_7f3a2b):
- auth-service: key lookup returned NotFound (key id not present) at 2026-03-04T21:02:13Z -> returned 401 to gateway
- shortly after, billing/quotas: spike in ingestion event for key abcxyz showing 15k tokens counted within 30s (suspicious; downstream consumer also showed normal traffic)
- gateway (route-policy): applied per-route burst limiter when backend error rate > 30% -> started returning 429 without Retry-After

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Transient datastore issue (etcd/cache) caused auth-service to fail key lookups briefly -> 401s. Gateway considered backend unhealthy -> enabled circuit-breaker/burst limiter -> 429s without retry headers.
2) Key rotation race: customer rotated key but some requests still using old key; however, other keys from same org unchanged and worked, so less likely.
3) Quota accounting bug: sudden double-counting of tokens triggered quota exhaustion and the system returned 429s. Explains 15k token spike in logs.
4) Malformed clients doing lots of retries causing rate-limit to trigger. Client telemetry didn’t show such behavior for this customer.

Reproduction steps I recommend for engineering to reproduce reliably:
- Simulate auth-store outage: bring up a test key and then flip a feature flag that makes auth-service return NotFound for ~45s. Run 10 concurrent clients with 1 req/s each. Observe 401 -> gateway-circuit -> 429s.
- Simulate double-counting: in staging, patch quota accounting to increment twice for a subset of requests and re-run the same traffic pattern.

Quick metrics / numbers (from admin/usage at time window):
- key: sk_live_customerABCxyz
- 2026-03-04 21:00-21:05 UTC -> reported tokens: 18320 (sudden jump)
- prior 5 minutes -> tokens: ~200
- requests: 420 requests in 5 minutes, error rate peaked at 38%

Temporary mitigations I tested or suggest: 
- Rotated customer key (issued new key, updated client) -> immediate reduction in 401s for the new key, but 429s persisted for a few minutes likely due to gateway cooldown.
- Whitelist key in gateway policy for 10 minutes (manual override) -> served traffic without 429s, allowed me to drain queued requests. Not long-term.
- Reverted feature flag in staging to validate auth-store resiliency patterns.

Notes on headers and diagnostics to instrument / look for next time: 
- Always log x-request-id and upstream request id at every layer (client, gateway, auth-service, quota service) and ensure sampling retention for 60 minutes around incidents.
- Log auth-store cache hit/miss ratio per key. If cache TTL eviction coincides with spike, we get noisy failures.
- Differentiate gateway 429s (no Retry-After) vs quota 429s (with Retry-After and x-rate-limit-*).
- Add metric: consecutive_401_count_by_key over sliding 2m window -> auto-escalate when > 5 for same key.

Questions / TODOs (who to loop in):
- @Ethan: can you dump the auth-service etcd health metrics around 2026-03-04 20:55-21:10 UTC? (JIRA-2148 assigned)
- @Samira: can you check if billing ingestion had any duplicate events from the ingestion pipeline? I saw a repeated token reporting batch at 21:01:02 UTC.
- SRE: consider a temporary rule to prefer 429 with Retry-After for gateway-limited responses so clients have explicit backoff.

Appendix: full curl trace (sanitized):
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (34.82.1.9) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> User-Agent: curl/7.88.1
> Accept: */*
> Authorization: Bearer sk_live_customerABCxyz
> Content-Type: application/json
> Content-Length: 39
>
* upload completely sent off: 39 out of 39 bytes
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2026 21:02:13 GMT
< Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
< Content-Length: 72
< Connection: keep-alive
< x-request-id: req_7f3a2b
<
{"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found"}}

Short-term checklist for next incident:
- Capture full curl traces with -v and save with timestamped file name.
- Immediately query admin/usage for the key to see token spikes.
- Capture gateway metrics: circuit-breaker events, backend health checks, rule evaluations.
- If 401s are widespread across keys -> suspect auth-store; if only one key -> suspect key management/rotation.

Final takeaway so far: auth-store flakiness + gateway circuit behavior is the most plausible root cause — transient 401s from NotFound propagated into gateway protective 429s that lacked official Retry-After headers. Next steps include running the auth-store outage sim, adding better logging, and re-evaluating gateway behavior to prefer informative 429s.

End of scratchpad.
